Subject: Renewal sequencing & co-terming proposal - BrightLeaf

Hi Stephanie —

Hope you had a good week. Our renewal for BrightLeaf is coming up (Dec 1) and Rajiv and I are trying to lock the term structure so we can finalize forecasting and procurement. We'd like to explore: a) multi-year pricing with an initial step-up ramp (lower year-1 capacity, higher in year-2/3), b) co-terming with one of our other vendor contracts that ends Mar 31, and c) an auto-renew option with a 60-day opt-out (helps our legal team with continuity).

High-level asks:
- Target A: 24–36 month term with a staged ramp (25% year-1, 50% year-2, 100% year-3 as baseline)
- Would Redwood offer a blended per-token price schedule for the ramp vs. full run-rate?
- Can we co-term to Mar 31 without losing price protections?
- Any standard language you recommend for the auto-renew opt-out window and renewal credits?

I've attached a basic rollforward doc showing our expected consumption and a forecast spreadsheet. Rajiv is looped for finance/legal constraints. Can we get a proposal this week? We have an internal procurement review on Nov 22.

Thanks,
Claire

Thanks Claire — appreciate the clear asks and the forecast. Initial thoughts below; I'll loop in Product and Pricing for proper numbers but wanted to get alignment on approach before we model.

- Multi-year + staged ramp: we can do a 3-year term with the staged ramp you outlined. We usually anchor discounts to an annual commit equivalent, then scale the effective per-token price across the ramp (year-1 higher effective per-token, tapering by year-3).
- Co-terming: co-terming to Mar 31 is doable. Two options: (A) true co-term where we prorate year-1 usage into the remainder period and keep the negotiated floor for the remainder, or (B) maintain the multi-year pricing but add a short cash/credit reconciliation to align invoicing windows. Option A keeps simplicity for you; option B gives more predictable revenue treatment for us.
- Auto-renew: 60-day opt-out is standard. We can include an auto-renew clause with a one-time renewal credit if usage grows 15%+ in the preceding term. We'll draft language you can share with procurement.

Next step: if you're comfortable with the approach above, I will draft a rollforward proposal and attach a model with blended per-token schedules. Marissa (product) and Karthik (finance/legal) are on the thread to sign off on the commercial/legal shapes. Can we target Nov 17 for a draft?

—Steph

Thanks — quick product/ops notes:

- We can reserve year-1 capacity at 25% of the year-3 baseline. We'll include an upsize trigger that allows BrightLeaf to convert reserved capacity into a higher commit within 30 days with pro-rated pricing.
- Co-terming option A (true co-term/prorate) is operationally simplest for BrightLeaf; we'll treat the remainder of the first year as a prorated tranche and apply the negotiated floor for the remaining co-term period. That avoids multiple invoices and simplifies reconciliation on your side.
- For billing, recommend a single invoice cadence aligned to Mar 31 after co-terming; finance will handle a one-time reconciliation credit for any difference between the original Dec 1 start and the co-term alignment.

Attached an initial model: RI_MultiYear_Prices_20261116.xlsx — it includes blended per-token tiers mapped to your forecast and two sample amortization approaches for the co-term alignment.

If this aligns, we can circulate a short amendment and a DocuSign packet for signature. Karthik — please validate the amendment language (auto-renew clause + 60-day opt-out + 15% growth credit).
